records.failed_witness: The first combined closeout patch exceeded the orchestration presentation budget and produced no attributable file mutation, so it earned zero closeout credit.
records.recovery: Inspect every intended path and strict-parse every existing JSON file before retrying, confirm that only the already-generated evidence owner manifest is pending, then apply the closeout records in bounded schema-aligned patches.
records.passing_witness: The bounded recovery proved that none of the intended closeout or seal files had been created or modified and that the worktree contained only the expected untracked evidence owner manifest before closeout resumed.
records.recurrence_guard: Split large multi-file patches into bounded schema groups and verify path existence, JSON parsing, and Git status after each group.
records.rollback: The failed patch created no closeout byte, Git object, ref, remote update, task message, or authority change and receives zero success credit.
records.sibling_recommendation: Prefer several small apply-patch operations for closeout packets and always inventory the worktree before retrying an interrupted edit.

records.failed_witness: The first bounded retry described each replacement as both a delete and an add in one apply-patch transaction, so patch verification rejected the operation before changing a file.
records.recovery: Use update operations for existing JSON records and add operations only for new paths, while retaining the rejected transaction at zero credit.
records.passing_witness: The corrected bounded update transaction changed exactly the three intended existing JSON records and left all other paths untouched.
records.recurrence_guard: Never target one path with multiple operation kinds inside a single apply-patch transaction.
records.rollback: The rejected patch changed no file, Git object, ref, remote, task route, or authority state and receives zero success credit.
records.sibling_recommendation: Separate update and add semantics explicitly when constructing multi-file closeout patches.

boundary: Post-evidence operational retention only. Bounded recovery establishes file-state facts, not independent reproduction, professional authority, empirical evidence, or permission to replay a successful canonical completion.
